chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ismail, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'What work do you engage in?' I said, 'I do not engage in any work these days.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Like that, your wealth will go away,' and it became difficult upon him.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of idleness on one's wealth according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses the example of Fuzayl ibn Yasar to illustrate the principle that active engagement in trade or work is essential for preserving wealth. The Imam’s sharp reaction to Fuzayl’s idleness underscores the Shia scholarly view that neglecting one’s livelihood is not merely a personal failing but a direct cause of financial loss, linking spiritual diligence with economic responsibility.
